subject: Partner dataflow & SLA stage gate — EU/APAC SI deployments

Subject: Discovery: EU/APAC SI deployments — initial dataflow map request

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. As discussed, Azura is preparing a regional delivery plan for enterprise customers in the EU and APAC that will use Redwood Dedicated nodes in-region, and we need to align on a stage-gate checklist before we kick off the first 3 pilots. High-level asks: 

- A target SLA matrix (latency P95, throughput, uptime) per region and per customer tier.
- A formal dataflow map we can attach to customer contracts documenting where tokens, logs, and KV caches will live and who controls keys.
- Any known constraints for EU data residency vs APAC (e.g., replication allowances, egress restrictions, KMS patterns).

Attached is a draft dataflow map from Azura (Azura_Dataflow_Map_v1.xlsx). Can your team confirm the fields we should expect from Redwood and call out any blocked elements that would affect an on-prem / VPC integration? Also, we'd prefer a short (1 page) staged acceptance criteria we can show legal and procurement.

Would you and Marissa be available for a 30-min alignment on Tuesday (Oct 27) EMEA morning?

Thanks,
Liam
—
Liam O'Connor
Head of Cloud Solutions, Azura Consulting

Liam —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick responses:

- We can produce a 1-page stage gate (acceptance criteria + minimal evidence) covering: connectivity, key management, audit logs, and failover/fallback behavior.
- For dataflow map fields, Redwood will provide: component location (region/zone), type of data stored (tokens, KV cache, telemetry), encryption-at-rest (customer KMS vs Redwood KMS), retention window, and redaction options.
- EU vs APAC differences: EU requires jurisdictional residency for logs/telemetry in several customers — we'll flag replication as "disallowed" unless customer signs a narrow cross-border consent. APAC customers often permit replication within approved regions but have stricter vendor audit requirements.

Sergio (copied) will take the technical lead on the dataflow mapping and confirm concrete bullet points for the stage gate doc. Marissa will help with the procurement/contract wording.

I can do Tue Oct 27 at 09:30 BST for a 30-min call — does that work for you?

Hannah

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-26T08:17:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: EU/APAC SI deployments — initial dataflow map request

Hi Liam —

I reviewed the Azura chart you sent. A few technical clarifications before we update our copy: 

1) Token residency: do you plan to surface raw model tokens back to Azura-managed systems, or only store encrypted KV caches locally? If the former, we need explicit customer consent for token storage and an approved handling SOP.

2) KMS: Azura's draft marks customer-managed KMS for EU. We support both models, but note that customer KMS in a VPC flow requires an HSM-backed key with cross-account IAM roles. Can you confirm the intended KMS topology (single customer key vs per-environment keys)?

3) Telemetry & logs: Which telemetry streams are considered PII for your customers? We typically segregate request metadata (non-PII) from content traces (PII) and we can switch telemetry to pseudonymized mode for pilot customers.

If you prefer, I can open a shared doc with line-by-line comments. I also attached a short SLA proposal (redwood-sla-proposal-2026.pdf) with suggested P95 latency and availability targets for Dedicated capacity in-region.

Regards,
Sergio

Attachment: redwood-sla-proposal-2026.pdf
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@azuraconsult.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Eun-Ji Park <eunji.park@eastbridge.com>, legal.ops@azuraconsult.com
Date: 2026-10-27T09:31:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: EU/APAC SI deployments — initial dataflow map request

Thanks, Sergio — answers inline below.

> 1) Token residency:
We will not store raw model tokens on Azura-managed systems for EU pilots. KV caches are local to customer VPCs and encrypted; any raw content traces are only retained by Azura for up to 7 days and then redacted per customer policy.

> 2) KMS:
Plan is per-customer keys (one key per environment) with Azura managing cross-account roles. If Redwood requires HSM-backed keys, that is acceptable — we'll surface that in the stage gate.

> 3) Telemetry & logs:
EastBridge customers classify prompts and outputs as regulated content — we'll flag those as PII. We will need Redwood to enable pseudonymization for those streams during pilot.

Let's take the answers into the call; 09:30 BST works. I'll upload a revised Azura_Dataflow_Map after the meeting.

—
Liam
